column1: # OUTSIDE_ISO_BASELINE.tsv -- PAT rejection tests (iso7185prt*) whose supposed violation is NOT an error in ISO 7185, so a conforming
# compiler ACCEPTS them and no rejection can be graded. CLASS not-an-iso-error. Ruled by the ceo, CEO-1231 (2026-09-24), on hq_pascal's
# ask q-pascal-pat-1834-and-1850-carry-no-iso-violation: they go OUTSIDE THE ISO BASELINE in the CEO-749 shape, printed by the runner
# and KEPT IN THE DENOMINATOR, so PAT reads x/427 OUTSIDE=2 and its ceiling is 425 by ruling. test_pascal_pat_suite.sh reads this file
# and cross-checks every listed program the other way round: SCRIP must ACCEPT it (a refusal is reported STALE and graded normally).
# Columns: program <TAB> CLASS <TAB> the measurement (Pascal-P5's own transcript, .ecp beside the program) <TAB> why ISO does not refuse it.
# EMPTIED 2026-09-25 by ceo CEO-1269 (hq_pascal's landing): iso7185prt1834 and iso7185prt1850 are no longer OUTSIDE -- fpc -Miso
# accepts both and runs them rc 0, so they are graded as ACCEPTANCE tests against its output; see ISO_ACCEPTS.tsv. The CEO-749
# mechanism above stays for any future program ISO 7185 does not make an error AND the oracle refuses.
